transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~45m
Location: Zoom
Recording: https://zoom.mock/recording/ff_20260506_oxbridge

Summary:
Quick renewal check-in to confirm Oxbridge's move from month-to-month to a 12-month retainer, scope additional capacity for 2x token throughput, and activate a UK-only region/VPC with KMS integration. Discussed tradeoffs between Dedicated capacity vs Hosted with VPC peering, and timeline for SOC2/audit artifacts. SE to run a short benchmark next week to validate latency for UK edge.

Topics Covered:
- Renewal term length and pricing levers
- Additional capacity: 2x baseline throughput and burst plan
- UK region onramp: VPC peering, KMS/HSM, audit logs, and data residency
- Dedicated pool vs hosted-with-VPC tradeoffs
- Pilot benchmark and go-live timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Mark (Redwood AE): Hey team, thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Sara (Oxbridge): Sara here. Hi.
[00:07] Tom (Oxbridge): Tom, hey.
[00:08] Liam (Oxbridge): Liam on procurement.
[00:09] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya, hi everyone.
[00:11] Mark: Sweet. Goal for today, real simple — confirm renewal terms, line up capacity, and walk through the UK sovereignty steps.

[00:35] Mark: Sara, quick context, you had mentioned a 2x throughput need and wanting UK-only residency for certain customers. Is that still the case?
[00:42] Sara: Yeah, still the ask. We have two product flows that are UK-only, and then broader EU flows. So ideally the UK model is isolated, keys don't leave region, that sort of thing.

[01:12] Priya: For that we'd typically recommend a VPC onramp paired with hosted private-control-plane or Dedicated depending on throughput needs. There's a couple of knobs — KMS integration, HSM if you need FIPS, and audit log retention.

[01:35] Tom: How big is the operational lift to go Dedicated vs Hosted with VPC peering? We don't want to add 6 months of ops work.

[01:44] Priya: Good question. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and simpler isolation, but provisioning GPUs and capacity takes a little longer and often a minimum commit. Hosted-with-VPC is faster to stand up, you get VPC peering and per-tenant routing, but you trade some absolute isolation and have different SLAs. For 2x throughput-during-peaks with burst, hosted-with-VPC plus reserved nodes for peak windows is something we see customers do to balance speed and cost.

[02:18] Sara: We're sensitive to cost but can't risk noisy neighbor. Are your tenancy guarantees for hosted-with-VPC explicit?

[02:25] Mark: Right now hosted-with-VPC uses logical isolation and routing policies; we can pin model versions and route by customer, but it's not per-GPU physical tenancy. We can propose a hybrid: reserved dedicated nodes for the UK flows that are most sensitive, and hosted for the rest.

[02:52] Liam: From procurement, any contract language about data residency? We need to add a clause that keys and PII processed in the UK stays there.

[03:01] Mark: Yes, we can add data residency clauses and show KMS key locality — we support customer-managed KMS currently and can note that keys are in UK region. We'll get legal to draft a specific addendum.

[03:20] Priya: Quick note — if you require HSM-backed keys and FIPS, that'll push an extra step in provisioning. It's common but adds lead time.

[03:34] Sara: We do need FIPS at least for card tokenization flows.

[03:39] Priya: OK noted. That typically moves us toward Dedicated or a Hosted path where we attach HSM in the region; we'll flag that in the runbook.

[04:05] Mark: Let's talk numbers briefly — right now your baseline commit is 50k tokens/minute (mock numbers) and you're asking for 2x baseline plus 3x burst windows. We sketched two options last week: (A) 12-month term with a 1.8x discount and burst credits, (B) 24-month with deeper discount. Which way are you leaning?

[04:36] Tom: We'd prefer 12 months to keep flexibility. But if pricing hits a certain per-token threshold we could do 24. Need details.

[04:45] Mark: Understood. I'll re-run pricing for 12 months including a Dedicated-hybrid top-up and send a sheet.

[05:05] Priya: From ops side, I recommend a short benchmark to validate latencies from UK to our nearest cluster. If we stand up UK region, we expect single-digit extra ms, but better to verify with your actual prompts. Can we run a 1-hour benchmark next week?

[05:25] Sara: Yes we can. We'll supply a sanitized prompt set.

[05:29] Priya: Great. I'll own that run and share results and recommended config.

[06:00] Mark: On timeline — if we get the signed PO by May 14, devops and SE can start the pilot the week of May 18, run benchmarks, then provision KMS and schedule cutover late May. That fits a June go-live for a limited set. Thoughts?

[06:22] Tom: That's aggressive but sounds doable. Need to confirm security review with our InfoSec team — they have a backlog.

[06:30] Sara: Also, can you surface SOC2 artifacts and pen-test reports? They'll ask.

[06:34] Mark: Yep. We have SOC2 Type II and recent penetration summary. I'll attach the doc pack.

[06:41] Liam: For procurement, when do you need a PO to lock pricing?

[06:45] Mark: Ideally May 14 to hit the provisioning window for late May. We'll honor pricing if PO is in draft by then.

[07:05] Priya: Small tech caveat — prefix/KV cache warms across model variants. If you pin model versions to the UK pool, cache priming is separate. For your chat models we recommend a short warm-up job post-provisioning.

[07:28] Sara: Ok. We have long contexts and frequent system messages; we care about cache behavior.

[07:35] Priya: Good note. We'll include recommended warm-up script in the ops bundle.

[08:00] Mark: Any blockers from legal or InfoSec right now?

[08:06] Tom: InfoSec wants encryption-at-rest verification and a timeline for HSM proof. Also they want to see audit logs retention policies.

[08:15] Mark: We can produce log retention configs and we have an audit logs export to your SIEM via S3 or syslog — we'll send sample configs.

[08:30] Liam: How about access control — SSO and RBAC? We need SCIM/SAML.

[08:36] Priya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Role-based access is configurable at account and team scopes.

[09:00] Sara: Another question — in a Dedicated setup, how does failover and cross-region routing work? If UK nodes have an outage, do requests fail to EU?

[09:14] Priya: You can define routing policies. We often configure automatic fallback to the nearest compatible model in EU with a lower SLO, or a queuing policy. We'll design a canary and fallback plan for you so critical flows keep running, albeit perhaps with different latency or model variant.

[09:38] Tom: We need the fallback documented and approved by InfoSec; automatic cross-border failover might be restricted for some datasets.

[09:47] Mark: Right — we can set a policy that prevents cross-border failover for UK-only datasets. It just means higher risk of an outage if region goes down. We'll surface that tradeoff in the runbook.

[10:10] Priya: On metrics, we'll provide dashboards for token spend, per-route latency, error rates, and KVS hit rates. You'll get per-model traces too.

[10:25] Sara: Great, those dashboards are important for ops.

[10:30] Mark: OK quick operational asks: Liam, procurement will need contract markup window; Tom, you will want InfoSec artifacts; Sara, SE will need prompt set for the benchmark. Agree?

[10:40] All: Yep.

[11:00] Priya: I'll propose the benchmark: 1 hour, 3 concurrent user profiles, your sanitized prompt set, record p95/p99 latencies and memory/KV hit rates. I'll send the test harness link.

[11:21] Sara: Can you include tokenization differences? We saw variance across model versions previously.

[11:25] Priya: Yes, will include token counts and per-model token cost estimates.

[11:40] Mark: Anything else on billing or invoicing?

[11:45] Liam: We prefer monthly invoicing with net-30; would like an annual commitment amortized monthly.

[11:52] Mark: That's fine. I will reflect amortized monthly billing on the pricing sheet.

[12:05] Tom: Competitor question — MegaCloud AI approached us with a lower headline price but no clear on-prem or UK HSM integration. If Redwood can show HSM + SOC2 pack that's a differentiator.

[12:20] Mark: Totally. We'll emphasize the KMS/HSM path and private VPC options in the renewal proposal.

[12:35] Sara: Also, show a rollback/fallback playbook; our platform team needs it.

[12:41] Priya: We'll attach a cutover and rollback checklist.

[13:00] Mark: OK let's recap actions — I'll send pricing and legal addendum; Priya will run benchmark and share ops doc; Sara to supply sanitized prompts; Liam will start purchase order process; Tom to coordinate InfoSec artifacts.

[13:20] Sara: Sounds good.

[13:25] Liam: Expected PO submission by May 11, maybe 14.

[13:30] Mark: Great. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark run. Thanks everyone.

[13:40] (call ends)
